title: Most People Miss This About Shame Entering the Story
paragraphs: Most People Miss This About Shame Entering the Story
They didn’t just eat the fruit.
They felt something break.

Silence fell.
Eyes opened.
And suddenly—they saw themselves.

Naked.
Exposed.
Uncovered.
That’s when shame entered the story.

Not when God spoke.
Not when judgment came.
But the moment sin twisted their vision.
“Then the eyes of both were opened… and they knew that they were naked.” (Genesis 3:7)
Catch this.

Before sin—no hiding.
After sin—covering.
They stitched fig leaves like bandages on a wound they couldn’t name.
And we’ve been doing the same ever since.

Different leaves.
Same shame.

Success to hide insecurity.
Filters to hide identity.
Silence to hide sin.
But here’s what we miss…
God didn’t walk away.
He walked toward them.
“Where are you?”

Not because He didn’t know.
But because they were lost in shame.
And here’s the holy tension—

The first question God asks fallen humanity
is not “What did you do?”
It’s “Where are you?”

Location before accusation.
Heart before behavior.
That’s grace… before the cross even appears.
But God doesn’t leave them in fig leaves.

He replaces their fragile covering
with something stronger.
Garments of skin. (Genesis 3:21)

Something had to die
to cover their shame.
That’s not random.
That’s a whisper of the Gospel.

Because one day,
Jesus Christ
would step into our nakedness…
take our shame…
and be stripped so we could be covered.

Not with leaves.
But with righteousness.
You’re not hiding from God.
You’re hiding because of shame.
And He’s still asking—
“Where are you?”

Not to expose you.
But to restore you.

Come out of the shadows.
Drop the leaves.
Let grace cover what shame tried to define.
Someone you know is still hiding.
